    • Seed germination → New life from "death"

    • Egg development → Easter eggs, new beginnings

    • Design tabletop protective packaging; no egg throwing/dropping or food prerequisite

    • Build bird houses (caring for creation)

    🙏 Liturgical Prayers for STREAM¶

    Opening Prayer (General)¶

    "Loving God, You created all things with wisdom and love. Open our minds to discover the wonders of Your creation. Help us use what we learn to serve others and give You glory. Amen."

    Advent STREAM Prayer¶

    "Lord Jesus, Light of the World, as we wait for Your coming, help us see Your presence in all we learn and create. May our work bring hope to others. Amen."

    Lenten STREAM Prayer¶

    "Merciful God, as we journey toward Easter, help us use our gifts to serve those in need. May we build with simplicity, create with purpose, and share with generosity. Amen."

    Easter STREAM Prayer¶

    "Risen Lord, You make all things new! As we explore Your creation, fill us with the joy of Easter. Help us see new life and new possibilities in everything we do. Alleluia! Amen."

    End-of-Year STREAM Prayer¶

    "Holy Spirit, thank You for the gifts of wonder, creativity, and learning. As we finish this year, help us carry what we've learned into the world, serving others with the talents You've given us. Amen."

    Budget and supply request templates¶

    Use the single Materials Plan and Inventory CSV; do not reuse the earlier inconsistent annual estimates, fixed loan claims or donor price promises. All costs are October 2026 planning estimates, NOT vendor quotations.

    Administration request (copy and complete)¶

    Date / to / from / school year: [ ]

    We request [configuration] for [number of cohorts] with capacity [up to 25 students per class]. The low-tech core supports individual observation, measurement, investigation, design/redesign, unplugged computing and authentic arts/music. Catholic identity informs dignity, truth, service and stewardship.

    Cost category Amount Evidence/assumption
    Goods, including first-year consumables [ ] Attach selected bill of materials
    Tax reserve [ ] 8% planning assumption; actual rate/exemption VERIFICATION REQUIRED
    Shipping reserve [ ] Confirm supplier/delivery
    Annual durable-replacement reserve [ ] Inspect equipment condition
    Total requested [sum] Below chosen ceiling; do not force spending
    Estimated recurring year-two total [ ] Separate from first-year total, using plan's cohort basis

    Conditional existing inventory: [Physical count/date/location and missing basics.] What is not covered: [All legacy lessons, specialty loans/apps, personal devices, simultaneous classrooms, extra cohorts unless costed.] Evaluation: [One named objective, individual prompt and evidence threshold; not unsupported achievement or recruitment promises.] Procurement/source questions: [Supplier specification/availability, electrical protection, ingredients, school privacy/license approval; VERIFICATION REQUIRED.]

    The school funds all required materials and work time. Donations and loans are optional enhancements, not prerequisites. Official Minnesota/Archdiocesan/NCEA alignment is claimed only after source verification.

    Quick reference: capacity 25 conditional configurations¶

    Ceiling Goods Tax Shipping Durable reserve First-year total
    $250 $194 $15.52 $10 $10 $229.52
    $500 $413 $33.04 $15 $15 $476.04
    $1,000 $754 $60.32 $20 $20 $854.32

    First three: one cohort, shared reusable equipment usable K-6 sequentially. Enhanced: seven sequential cohort consumable allocations plus conditional standalone robots, not a fleet of managed tablets. See full arithmetic, year-two totals, exact kits and battery assumptions in the plan.

    Grant / donor / optional donation copy¶

    Grant summary: "We seek [amount] for [specific materials/objectives/cohorts]. We will document [individual evidence] and inspect/replenish kits annually." Do not invent baseline results, grant eligibility or official accreditation.

    Optional donation: "Clean, dry flat cardboard is welcome after teacher screening. Donating is optional; every child has school-provided supplies. Please send no batteries, magnets, glass, sharp metal, latex or chemical/food-soiled containers." No suggested dollar level promises a month/semester of lessons.

    Thank-you: "Thank you for [confirmed contribution]. It supported [actual learning/material use]." Photographs require verified consent. Tax deductibility, school legal status, gift-processing arrangements and monetary donation instructions are VERIFICATION REQUIRED with administration.

    STREAM Night & Family Event Guide¶

    {: .no_toc }

    Table of Contents¶

    {: .no_toc .text-delta }

    1. TOC

    Overview¶

    STREAM Night is a celebration of student learning that brings families together to experience hands-on Science, Technology, Religion, Engineering, Art, and Math activities. This guide provides everything you need to plan a successful STREAM Night or family showcase event at Our Lady of the Prairie Catholic School.

    October 2026 operating conditions: C is Catholic identity, R is explicit religion/faith integration, A includes arts/music, and M is mathematics. This optional event celebrates in-school learning; no home-built project, purchased display board, family attendance or donation affects grades. Use the family copy system and objective-linked rubric. Event costs below are separate planning estimates, not vendor quotes or part of the core classroom budgets. Re-cost for actual attendance, tax and shipping. Confirm staffing, venue capacity, accommodations, safeguarding and photo/consent procedures with the school. Scripture quotations and Church attributions below are VERIFICATION REQUIRED before printing; devotional symbolism is not scientific evidence.

    SAFETY: No button cells, latex balloons or projectile stations; no neodymium magnets in K. Adults manage electrical power, small parts and safe bounded tests. Close unstaffed hazardous stations rather than assuming volunteers will arrive. Plan an indoor January version and accessible seated/silent routes. Suspected battery/magnet ingestion or other urgent danger triggers immediate school emergency escalation. Use counted kits.

    Why Host a STREAM Night?¶

    Benefit Description
    Family Engagement Parents experience what their children learn
    Student Pride Children showcase their work and explain their thinking
    Community Building Strengthens school-family-parish connections
    Faith Integration Demonstrates how faith and reason work together
    STEM Excitement Generates enthusiasm for STEM learning
    Recruitment Attracts prospective families to your school

    Event Format Options¶

    Option 1: Student Showcase (Recommended for First Event)¶

    Duration: 90 minutes
    Best For: Displaying student work from throughout the year

    Structure:

    • Students stand by their projects

    • Families rotate through displays

    • Students explain their work to visitors

    • Interactive elements at each station

    Option 2: Interactive STREAM Stations¶

    Duration: 2 hours
    Best For: Hands-on family experiences

    Structure:

    • 6-8 activity stations around the space

    • Families rotate every 15-20 minutes

    • Each station has a hands-on challenge

    • Volunteers facilitate each station

    Option 3: STREAM Fair (Competition Format)¶

    Duration: 3 hours
    Best For: Older students (grades 3-6)

    Structure:

    • Students complete assessed work during school; optional home conversation only

    • Projects displayed using school paper/models; purchased boards not required

    • Judges evaluate using rubrics

    • Awards ceremony at conclusion

    Option 4: Family Engineering Night¶

    Duration: 90 minutes
    Best For: Maximum participation

    Structure:

    • Families work together on challenges

    • All families do the same activity simultaneously

    • Emphasis on teamwork and fun

    • Simple, no-pressure format

    Planning Timeline¶

    8 Weeks Before Event¶

    Week 8 Tasks:

    • Choose event date (check parish/school calendar)

    • Select event format

    • Reserve venue (gym, cafeteria, parish hall)

    • Create planning committee

    • Set budget with administration

    • Begin promoting to families

    Committee Roles: | Role | Responsibilities | |------|------------------| | Event Coordinator | Overall planning, communication | | Volunteer Coordinator | Recruit and train helpers | | Setup/Cleanup Lead | Room arrangement, teardown | | Materials Manager | Gather and organize supplies | | Technology Support | Projector, music, slideshow | | Hospitality Lead | Refreshments, welcome table |

    6 Weeks Before Event¶

    Week 6 Tasks:

    • Send "Save the Date" to families

    • Recruit volunteers (need 10-15 for medium event)

    • Identify which projects/activities to feature

    • Order any special supplies

    • Coordinate with parish for opening prayer leader

    • Plan refreshments (simple is fine!)

    4 Weeks Before Event¶

    Week 4 Tasks:

    • Send detailed invitation with RSVP

    • Create station activity plans

    • Confirm volunteer assignments

    • Design event signage

    • Plan any student presentations

    • Arrange for photographer (yearbook staff?)

    2 Weeks Before Event¶

    Week 2 Tasks:

    • Finalize volunteer schedule

    • Gather all materials

    • Create instruction cards for each station

    • Print student name tags

    • Prepare display boards

    • Send reminder to families

    Week of Event¶

    Final Preparation:

    • Confirm RSVP numbers

    • Organize materials by station

    • Create room layout map

    • Prepare volunteer packets

    • Test all technology

    • Set up welcome/registration table materials

    Day of Event¶

    Setup (2 hours before):

    • Arrange tables and stations

    • Post directional signs

    • Set up student work displays

    • Prepare each activity station

    • Brief all volunteers

    • Test audio/visual equipment

    • Set out refreshments

    Activity Station Ideas¶

    Station 1: Tower Building Challenge¶

    Faith Connection: Building our faith on a strong foundation

    Item Details
    Materials Large blocks, folded paper or dry cups; no food prerequisite
    Challenge Build the tallest tower in 10 minutes
    Scripture "Built on the rock" (Matthew 7:24-27)
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1 facilitator

    Station 2: Coding Corner¶

    Faith Connection: God gave us creativity and problem-solving minds

    Item Details
    Materials Preapproved tested devices only if confirmed; large arrow cards and desk grids for a separate unplugged concept activity
    Challenge Complete a coding puzzle or program a robot
    Scripture "For we are God's handiwork" (Ephesians 2:10)
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1-2 helpers

    Station 3: Tabletop Simple Machines¶

    Faith Connection: Using knowledge responsibly to help others

    Item Details
    Materials Enclosed classroom pulley, short cord, light teacher-controlled desk-level load
    Challenge Compare how the pulley changes the direction of a gentle pull; no launching or overhead loads
    Source status Faith-source wording VERIFICATION REQUIRED; no forced Scripture analogy
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1 facilitator

    Station 4: Bridge Building¶

    Faith Connection: Building bridges to serve others

    Item Details
    Materials Paper/cardboard, rulers, stable supports, ten index cards per team for controlled tests
    Challenge Compare two bridge forms using the same gap and counted cards; no uncontrolled heavy weights
    Scripture "Bear one another's burdens" (Galatians 6:2)
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1 facilitator

    Station 5: Art & Math Symmetry¶

    Faith Connection: Finding God's patterns in creation

    Item Details
    Materials Graph paper, colored pencils, symmetry cards
    Challenge Create symmetrical designs
    Scripture "He has made everything beautiful" (Ecclesiastes 3:11)
    Volunteer Needed Optional

    Station 6: Science Discovery¶

    Faith Connection: Exploring God's wonderful creation

    Item Details
    Materials Magnifying glasses, nature items, microscopes
    Challenge Observe and draw what you discover
    Scripture "The heavens declare the glory of God" (Psalm 19:1)
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1 facilitator

    Station 7: Circuit Creations¶

    Faith Connection: Being a light to the world

    Item Details
    Materials Verified protected switched 2-AA packs, current-limited 3-V LED modules and insulated leads; adult-managed cells
    Challenge Complete a circuit to light up an LED
    Scripture "You are the light of the world" (Matthew 5:14)
    Volunteer Needed Yes - 1 helper

    Station 8: Prayer & Reflection¶

    Faith Connection: Center of our STREAM learning

    Item Details
    Materials Prayer cards, journals, quiet seating
    Activity Write a prayer of thanks for God's creation
    Scripture Various creation and wonder verses
    Volunteer Needed Optional

    Teach Students to Say: 1. "Hi! My name is _____ and I'm in ___ grade." 2. "This is my _____ project." 3. "I made this by..." 4. "I learned that..." 5. "Do you have any questions?"

    • Present to another classroom

    • Optional conversation at home; all required rehearsal happens in class

    • Role-play with teacher

    Faith Integration Ideas¶

    Opening Prayer¶

    Creator God,

    Thank you for the gift of wonder and curiosity. Thank you for the minds You have given us to explore Your creation.

    Tonight, we celebrate learning together as a community. Help us see Your hand in science, technology, engineering, art, and math.

    Bless our families as they discover and create together. May everything we learn draw us closer to You.

    We ask this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

    Closing Prayer¶

    Loving God,

    Thank you for this time together as a school family. We are grateful for our students and all they have learned. We are grateful for our teachers who guide them with faith and love. We are grateful for families who support learning at home.

    As we go home tonight, help us continue to wonder, to question, and to discover. May we use our talents to serve others and glorify You.

    We ask this in Jesus' name. Amen.

    Volunteer Information¶

    Volunteer Roles Needed¶

    Role Number Duties
    Welcome/Registration 2 Greet families, hand out maps
    Station Facilitators 6-8 Guide activity at assigned station
    Floaters 2-3 Help where needed, manage supplies
    Cleanup Crew 4-6 Post-event teardown
    Photographer 1 Capture the event
    Refreshment Host 2 Manage food/drinks

    Volunteer Briefing Script¶

    Read to volunteers before event:

    "Thank you for helping with STREAM Night! Here are a few things to remember:

    1. Be welcoming - Smile and greet every family
    2. Encourage participation - Offer accessible choices and confirmed station capacity; do not require every activity
    3. Let kids lead - Guide, don't take over
    4. Keep it positive - There's no wrong way to explore
    5. Connect to faith - Use the scripture signs as conversation starters
    6. Watch the clock - Help families move when it's time
    7. Have fun! - Your enthusiasm is contagious

    Questions? Find me (Event Coordinator) in the _____ area."

    Troubleshooting Common Issues¶

    Low Registration Numbers¶

    Solutions:

    • Send personal reminders

    • Have students invite grandparents

    • Partner with parish events

    • Offer incentives (raffle prize for attendees)

    • Simplify the event to reduce intimidation

    Not Enough Volunteers¶

    Solutions:

    • Reduce number of stations

    • Ask 8th graders or Confirmation students to help

    • Partner with Knights of Columbus or other parish groups

    • Have teachers facilitate instead of parents

    Running Out of Supplies¶

    Solutions:

    • Have backup simple activities ready

    • Set limits per family at each station

    • Cross-train floaters to help manage supplies

    • Focus on reusable materials

    Crowd Management¶

    Solutions:

    • Use timed rotations with a bell/announcement

    • Assign families to starting stations

    • Have clear directional signs

    • Position greeters at each area

    Technology Issues¶

    Solutions:

    • Test everything day before

    • Have paper backups for coding activities

    • Bring extra batteries

    • Ensure good WiFi or offline alternatives

    After the Event¶

    Thank You Notes¶

    Send within one week:

    • Thank volunteers personally

    • Send note home to all families

    • Thank administration and parish support

    • Acknowledge any sponsors

    Documentation¶

    • Collect photos from volunteers/families

    • Write brief summary for newsletter

    • Note what worked well

    • Note what to improve

    • Save materials list for next year

    • Store reusable supplies properly

    Evaluation Questions¶

    Ask Planning Committee: 1. What went really well? 2. What would we do differently? 3. Did families seem engaged? 4. Were there any safety concerns? 5. Was the timeline appropriate? 6. What feedback did you hear from families?

    Templates

    C-STREAM templates¶

    October 2026 formats for K-6; complete bracketed fields before teaching. Native periods: K 25, grades 1-2 30, grades 3-4 40, grades 5-6 45 minutes.

    C is Catholic identity; R is religion/faith integration; A is arts including music; M is mathematics. Art includes observation, composition, design, performance and communication without a screen; it is not merely decoration. Only claim domains genuinely practiced. All required work and supplies are provided at school; no routine homework or donation prerequisites.

    Creating... Use What it protects
    One meeting Lesson plan At a glance, background/vocabulary, native timings, safety, scaling and individual evidence
    A unit Cross-curricular unit Prerequisites, meeting sequence, balance, logistics, family copy
    Multi-meeting project PBL overlay Launch/research/create/present using the same unit and lesson formats
    Student response Student sheet Show/tell/draw or record; nonreader route
    Substitute handoff Substitute lesson 20-minute preparation gate and named fallbacks
    Individual evidence Assessment Objective -> prompt -> success condition -> student evidence
    ¾-level criteria Rubric Observable objective-linked levels, not participation or polish
    Family copy Newsletter Actual learning and optional no-purchase conversation/activity
    Materials/kit Materials list Normalized items, 10/15/20/25 quantities and replenishment
    Standards evidence Standards mapping Local catalog and separately verified official alignment

    The local 18-code catalog defines CST-C1..C3, CST-S1..S3, CST-T1..T3, CST-E1..E3, CST-A1..A3 and CST-M1..M3. Do not generate new local codes or label these official Archdiocesan/Minnesota standards. Official source questions remain VERIFICATION REQUIRED.

    Operational entry points: materials, technology, substitutes, family communication, rubrics, student resources.

    C-STREAM lesson plan template¶

    Version 3.0 - October 2026. Copy and complete this format; bracketed fields are author prompts, not finished instructions. Preserve a useful existing lesson, its URL and learning purpose when bringing it into this format.

    C = Catholic identity; S = science; T = technology (tools and computing); R = religion/faith integration; E = engineering; A = arts, including visual art, design and music; M = mathematics, not music. Catholic identity informs purpose, dignity, truth and stewardship throughout. R names the explicit faith teaching/reflection. Art must involve an artistic decision, observation, composition or communication, not simply decorating a STEM product. Emphasize only domains students actually practice; do not claim all seven in every lesson.

    Lesson at a glance¶

    Field Complete before teaching
    Grade; rotation; schedule; unit; title [K/½/¾/⅚; A/B; weekly/bi-weekly; unit; title]
    Time [K 25 / grades 1-2 30 / grades 3-4 40 / grades 5-6 45 minutes]
    Big idea; why learn this? [Concept and everyday/service/vocation application]
    Learning objective O1 "I can [observable action + concept + success condition]."
    Optional O2 [Second objective only if teachable and assessable in this period]
    C-STREAM areas addressed [C/S/T/R/E/A/M and actual student action for each claimed domain]
    Catholic connection [A concrete design/ethical/stewardship decision; not prayer alone]
    Faith source/status [Primary-source URL, section, paraphrase/quotation status; VERIFICATION REQUIRED if unresolved]
    Local standards [Select from the 18-code catalog in the standards mapping section below]
    Official alignment [Verified source/benchmark/version, or VERIFICATION REQUIRED; never infer from a title]
    Technology Requirement [None / Optional / Recommended / Required; justification]
    Difficulty; prerequisites [Introductory/developing/complex; prior skills to check]
    Teacher prep [Exact minutes; Minimal <5, Light 5-15, Moderate >15-30, Significant >30]
    Cleanup [Minutes INCLUDED in the class period]
    Kit/location; readiness [Kit ID; actual location filled by school; tested by/date; unresolved blockers]

    3. [Perform the exact teacher prep test, including the expected result.]
    4. [Set up tables/trays and demonstrate safe boundaries before distribution.]
    5. [Post/draw the objective and two or three visual steps; read them aloud.]
    6. [Prepare the indoor/no-device/missing-supply fallback and individual check.]

    Do not invent a closet location, school account, app license or loan reservation. No routine homework and no donation prerequisite.

    Word (teach 2-4) Plain-language definition Object/picture/gesture

    • [Specific hazards, age restrictions, teacher-only steps and stop signal.]

    • Never use button cells, latex balloons or projectile activities in this core program. No neodymium magnets in K; use large encapsulated ferrite magnets only where age-appropriate. Keep all small parts inaccessible to children who mouth objects. Use protected AA circuit packs; no mains power or exposed hot components.
    • [What to do for a spill, injury, missing battery/magnet, overheated component.] Stop, isolate the activity and contact the school's responsible adult/emergency procedure. A possible swallowed battery or magnet needs urgent emergency escalation, not a classroom troubleshooting attempt.
    • Indoor alternative: [Equivalent objective and setup; no unsafe cold exposure.]

    Exact lesson sequence¶

    The following allocations total the native period and protect test/redesign, individual evidence and cleanup. Choose ONE column; replace actions with exact directions and materials. Do not add untimed prayer, transitions or worksheets.

    Step K: 25 1-2: 30 3-4: 40 5-6: 45 Teacher says/does; student action
    1. Hook, purpose, Catholic connection 0-3 0-3 0-4 0-4 "[Actual question]"; [brief prayer if appropriate]
    2. Vocabulary, model and safety 3-7 3-8 4-10 4-11 [Demonstrate one complete action; ask a check question]
    3. Plan and build/investigate 7-14 8-18 10-24 11-27 [Numbered, concrete directions; rotate builder/tester/reporter]
    4. Test, compare and improve 14-19 18-23 24-32 27-36 [Same test conditions; one evidence-based change and retest]
    5. Individual objective-linked check 19-22 23-27 32-37 36-41 [Each child shows/tells/draws O1; record evidence]
    6. Cleanup and close 22-25 27-30 37-40 41-45 [Count, sort, disconnect, dry and return; closing thought]

    Questions to ask: "[What changed?]"; "[What stayed the same?]"; "[What evidence supports your choice?]"; "[Who does this design include?]"; "[How did you avoid waste?]" Supply topic-specific versions, not just "facilitate discussion."

    K-1/nonreader directions: [Show the real object, say ONE step, let students do it, repeat. Use pointing, sorting, building, gesture and dictated evidence.]

    What success looks like / individual assessment¶

    Objective Individual prompt/task Meets expectation Evidence/mode Local code
    O1 [Actual exit question/demo] [Observable threshold] [Teacher roster: each child's response, not team product alone] [ ]
    O2 if taught [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Use assessment and rubric formats. Levels: 1 Beginning, 2 Developing, 3 Meets Expectation, 4 Extends Learning; NE = not yet evidenced, not a zero. Participation, handwriting, neatness, confidence and artistic talent are not proxies for O1. Score an arts criterion only when that arts skill is an explicit objective.

    At 25 students, gather a quick simultaneous point/show/draw response and use a planned roster sweep during hands-on time. If oral conferences need more time, record NE and schedule a check next meeting; never claim all were assessed. At expected-mastery checkpoints, Local Standards requires two dated observations on separate occasions with an individual demonstration and changed context/follow-up explanation. One exit check alone does not establish end-of-grade mastery.

    Support and challenge¶

    Support: [Read aloud; fewer choices; pre-cut pieces; larger tools; bilingual vocabulary/gesture; seated/quiet option; adult scribing. Keep the same concept unless explicitly documenting an objective change.]

    Challenge: [Add a justified constraint, repeat trial, compare data, or explain a tradeoff. Do not routinely turn faster learners into helpers.]

    Problem Exact response Objective preserved or changed?
    Structure/test fails [Stabilize supports; change one variable; record failure as evidence] [ ]
    Supplies missing [Named safe substitution, quantity and changed constraint] [ ]
    Devices/network/loan unavailable [Unplugged task or reschedule] Programming/robot operation needs later real-device evidence
    Early finishers [Specific extension] [ ]
    Time short Stop new building; keep individual check and cleanup; continue later [Unfinished evidence recorded]
    Unsafe condition Stop affected activity; safe seated fallback; notify responsible adult [Do not silently continue]

    Cleanup, family communication and follow-up¶

    1. [Stop tests; switch off/disconnect packs; teacher counts hazardous parts.]
    2. [Sort reusable vs waste; dry all wet materials; wipe tables per school practice.]
    3. [Restock exact quantities; label broken kit OUT OF SERVICE and report.]
    4. [Record elapsed time, individual evidence, supply use and next reteach.]

    Copy the newsletter block. Include what children did/learned, a Catholic connection, a specific oral question, and an optional no-purchase activity. No routine homework.

    Standards mapping¶

    Use only the local catalog: CST-C1/C2/C3, CST-S1/S2/S3, CST-T1/T2/T3, CST-E1/E2/E3, CST-A1/A2/A3, CST-M1/M2/M3. Definitions and grade expectations belong to Local Standards, not this template. Use Standards Mapping for the chain standard -> grade -> unit -> lesson -> objective -> individual evidence.

    Ready-to-teach check¶

    • Native timings sum correctly, including cleanup.
    • Complete kit and scaling confirmed for actual enrollment.
    • Teacher background, model, safety, misconceptions and failure responses supplied.
    • Each assessed objective has an individual prompt and success condition.
    • Support, challenge, indoor and no-device contingencies are explicit.
    • Faith/source claims accurate or marked VERIFICATION REQUIRED.
    • Family copy prepared; no home purchase, donation or device prerequisite.
    • Substitute has named contact and actual materials location.

    Project-based learning template¶

    Use the unit template as the planning record and lesson template for each meeting. This project overlay preserves Launch -> Research -> Create -> Present without creating a competing lesson format. Version 3.0 - October 2026.

    Project at a glance¶

    • Title / grade K-6 / A-B rotation / weekly or bi-weekly: [ ]
    • Driving question: "How can we [specific problem] for [intended user]?"
    • Meetings / native period / due date: [K 25, 1-2 30, 3-4 40, 5-6 45 minutes]
    • Big idea / why this matters / prerequisites: [ ]
    • Objectives O1/O2 / local standards / individual final evidence: [ ]
    • C Catholic identity / R sourced faith reflection: [Purpose, dignity, stewardship, truth or service influences an actual decision.]
    • A arts (including music) / M mathematics: [Specific artistic and math actions, if claimed; music is within A, not the M abbreviation.]
    • Technology Requirement: [None / Optional / Recommended / Required, per meeting; why and what changes without it.]
    • Prep / cleanup / difficulty / kit-location: [Exact minutes and confirmation]

    Project phases¶

    Phase Linked native-period meeting(s) Student work Individual evidence/checkpoint
    Launch and wonder [ ] Identify user need, criteria and constraints; predict Each child names/shows the problem
    Research and learning [ ] Classroom source/model or investigation; collect evidence Each child explains one finding
    Create and iterate [ ] Plan, build, fair test, revise and retest Each child explains a result and resulting change
    Present and reflect [ ] Communicate evidence to a class audience Each child demonstrates O1; teacher uses linked criteria

    Criteria, responsibilities and access¶

    Success criteria: [Measurable conditions, not "beautiful," "creative" or "participates well."] Constraints: [Time, materials, safety, cost.] Team roles/rotation: [Builder/tester/reporter; each child gets a hands-on turn.] Individual deliverable: [Show/tell/draw/record; use the student sheet or nonreader card rather than a mandatory written report.] Arts objective if used: [Composition, pattern, observation, musical phrase or visual communication; assess the named skill rather than expensive presentation.]

    Complete the unit's materials/safety/support/challenge/fallback sections, including 10/15/20/25 scaling, teacher-only prep, exact test and cleanup. Retain records between meetings in labeled bins; no fragile work transported home as a requirement. School supplies and work time cover participation.

    Catholic purpose and service¶

    • Who might benefit? [An authentic, respectfully described user need.]
    • Which decision honors dignity or care for creation? [Actual example.]
    • Faith source: [Primary URL/section; VERIFICATION REQUIRED if unverified.]
    • Classroom model vs actual service: [Do not claim a prototype has helped people without evidence. Do not deploy assistive/medical/structural devices or drinking-water filters without qualified adult review.]
    • Optional visitors, parish partnerships and events need confirmation and a school-run alternative; they are not prerequisites.

    Assessment and family copy¶

    Use the assessment template and student project rubric. Share 1-3 objective-linked criteria before launch. No universal 100-point or faith/ presentation weighting. Technical evidence and faith reasoning remain distinguishable; neither team success nor enthusiasm proves individual mastery.

    Use the newsletter template at launch and completion. No routine homework, home research, donation, purchased board, family attendance or personal device required. Optional no-purchase family conversation: "[One actual question a child can answer orally.]"

    Before reuse¶

    Record observed prep/cleanup minutes, consumables per cohort, individual evidence still missing, unsafe/missing parts, verified sources, objective changes and revisions. Use Standards Mapping to connect only practiced standards from Local Standards.

Activities at home are optional, no-purchase and ungraded. Record actual outcomes, supply consumption, source questions, individual reteaching and changes needed before reuse.

    Nonreader and substitute route¶

    Use the actual Show, Try, Tell card. The adult shows the object or picture, says one instruction, models it, then lets each child act. Child points/builds/sorts/gestures/tells; adult records the child's words or action. Do not hand a nonreader this text and expect independent reading. Use a larger object or scribe without changing the conceptual criterion.

    No handwriting, neatness, enthusiasm or drawing-skill score unless that skill is the explicit objective. Store named evidence under actual school practice, not public newsletters or an invented digital account.

    This is a cover sheet for a completed lesson plan, not a claim that all legacy lessons are substitute-ready.

    At a glance¶

    Grade/unit/title/date/rotation: [ ] Full lesson link: [ ] Native period: [25/30/40/45] Objective O1 and individual check: [ ] Big idea/why/Catholic connection: [ ] Vocabulary (2-4) and background/misconception: [Short plain-language notes.] Local code/source status: [Link to Local Standards; official alignment/source questions VERIFICATION REQUIRED.] Technology Requirement: [None/Optional/Recommended/Required + reason.] Difficulty/prep/cleanup: [Exact minutes; cleanup included in period.] Kit label/actual location/contact: [School fills in, not "likely in closet."]

    Prep window Action Stop condition
    0-4 Read objective, sequence, background and individual success condition Instructions or criterion missing
    4-8 Locate/count student/team/class/teacher materials; verify 10/15/20/25 quantities Required kit absent/short
    8-12 Read safety; review accommodations and school emergency contact; inspect equipment Unverified hazard or damage

    16-20 Draw/read aloud steps; rehearse assessment, cleanup and fallback No feasible native-period plan

    If a stop condition occurs, tell the office/regular teacher and use the safe fallback, recording changed objectives. No repairing electrical gear, hunting personal accounts or going outdoors in unsafe weather.

    Assessment template¶

    Grade/unit/lesson/date: [ ] Objective O1: [Observable action + concept + condition.] Local code: [From Local Standards.]

    Objective Actual individual prompt/task Success condition When/how collected Allowed mode/support
    O1 "[Question]" / [Demonstration] [Number, unit, correct comparison, evidence or explanation required] [During test/exit; minutes] [Show/tell/draw/scribe/record]

    Example, not an official grade benchmark: O1 compare two paper structures under the same load. Prompt: "Show which held the load, and what stayed the same in your test." Meets: identifies the observed result and keeps span/load placement the same. A failed bridge can supply valid evidence.

    Student Actual evidence, not "good work" Objective Level ½/¾ or NE Access support Feedback/next check
    [ ] [ ] O1 [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Use Rubric Template. NE means not yet evidenced; absence, missed observation or equipment failure does not prove low mastery. Ordinary access accommodations do not cap a score. Distinguish a conceptual hint from read-aloud, translation, scribing or motor assistance.

    Collect a response from every child; a group prototype is supporting evidence, not an individual score. At 25, observe nine teams during hands-on work plus simultaneous exit responses. Mark any unobserved child NE and arrange a brief next-meeting check. Give one specific feedback statement and one next action. Do not average unrelated objectives or replace learning evidence with participation, prayer behavior, confidence or attractive displays.

    Expected-mastery checkpoints: Follow Local Standards: at least two dated observations on separate occasions, including an individually attributable demonstration and a changed context or follow-up explanation; both meet the grade target. A single lesson's level 3 is that occasion's evidence, not end-of-grade mastery. Record NE/not yet assessed when evidence is missing and schedule the next check.

    Device objective: [Record actual program execution/robot action if required. Paper algorithm evidence does not establish programming mastery.] Faith objective if assessed: [Reasoned choice/understanding of taught content, not strength of belief, prayer frequency or family practice.] Official alignment: [Verified URL/version/benchmark or VERIFICATION REQUIRED.]

    Objective-linked rubric template¶

    Grade/unit/lesson: [ ] Objective/code: [ ] Prompt: [ ] Modes/support: [Show/tell/draw/record, read-aloud/scribe/larger materials.] Select 1-3 criteria genuinely taught. State the Meets condition first.

    Criterion linked to objective 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning (optional)
    [Observable concept/action] [Evidence reveals named misconception or missing action] [Partial evidence; specify missing part] [Exact success condition] [Transfers/explains using additional evidence; not beyond-grade content by default]

    For a three-level rubric omit column 4; do not relabel NE as Beginning. NE: not yet evidenced sits outside the scale.

    Completed example¶

    O1: Compare flat and folded paper using an equal span and load.

    Criterion 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning
    Evidence-based comparison Names a result different from the observed test Names the observed stronger design but cannot identify the common test condition yet Names the observed result and shows equal span and load placement Repeats the fair test and explains whether the second result supports the first

    A collapsed bridge can still meet this objective. Decorative skill, participation, handwriting, family help and confident speech are not this criterion. If the objective is a rhythmic pattern or visual composition, write a separate arts criterion measuring that named artistic decision, not "looks beautiful." Assess Catholic reasoning from taught content, not a child's interior faith.

    Scoring/evidence record: use Assessment Template. One Meets rating is evidence for that occasion. Expected-mastery checkpoints require two dated observations on separate occasions under Local Standards, not one polished project. Source/status: local teacher criterion; official standards alignment requires verification in Standards Mapping.

    Use Materials Plan and Inventory CSV. School funds the required materials; donations are optional and screened, never a student prerequisite.

    Standards mapping template¶

    The definitions belong to Local Standards. The 18 local codes are CST-C1/C2/C3, CST-S1/S2/S3, CST-T1/T2/T3, CST-E1/E2/E3, CST-A1/A2/A3 and CST-M1/M2/M3. R faith integration is recorded with the Catholic domain; music belongs to A. Do not invent CST-R or music-as-M codes.

    Local code Grade Rotation/schedule Unit Lesson link Objective Student action Individual assessment/evidence Intro/develop/reinforce/expected Evidence status
    [Catalog code] [K-6] [ ] [ ] [Actual path] O1 [ ] [ ] [Actual question/demo + success condition] [Per progression, not guess] [Verified document / observed classroom / VERIFICATION REQUIRED]

    Only claim a code when students practice its defined competency; topic keywords alone are insufficient. Record individual evidence even for team products.

    Official alignment is a separate claim¶

    Authority/framework Version/applicable year Exact benchmark/code/text or paraphrase Primary URL/document/section Lesson evidence Verified by/date/status
    [Minnesota / Archdiocese / CSTA / other] [ ] [Do not invent] [ ] [ ] [VERIFICATION REQUIRED until checked]

    Local codes are not official Archdiocesan or state standards. Consult the shared review's source record; source or Church quotation questions remain VERIFICATION REQUIRED until checked against the primary document.

    Music is a genuine part of A in C-STREAM, but the local catalog chiefly defines visual observation/design/communication and does not certify full music standards coverage. Map a music task only where its action actually meets a catalog competency; verify any official music benchmark separately. Do not create a music-as-M code or invent an extra local domain.

    Rubrics

    C-STREAM rubrics¶

    October 2026 revision: lightweight ¾-level evidence rather than universal 100-point weighting. State the objective, prompt and Meets condition first. NE = not yet evidenced, not a zero or proof of low mastery.

    Need Resource Audience
    Project science/design/math/arts evidence Student project rubric Teacher/student; each child demonstrates learning
    Reasoning, communication or taught collaboration skill Skills assessment Teacher; observable actions, not personality
    Taught dignity/service/stewardship reasoning Service rubric Teacher/student; no compulsory external service
    Quality/accuracy of faith integration in a lesson Faith-reason rubric Teacher/administrator; NOT a student belief score
    Write a specific criterion Rubric template Lesson author; three or four levels
    Record each child's evidence Assessment template Teacher; prompt, evidence, feedback, next check

    Assessment measures the stated objective, not participation, handwriting, neatness, presentation expense or confidence. An arts criterion assesses a named composition/design/performance skill only if taught as an objective. Accept show/tell/draw/scribe/record with access supports. Failed models can provide excellent evidence; a working group product does not establish every child's mastery. Never grade prayer habits, family religion or interior belief.

    Use the 18 local codes with actual lesson evidence. Official standards/Church quotation claims require source verification. Do not equate a rubric score with complete official curriculum alignment.

    Faith-reason integration lesson-quality rubric¶

    Audience: teachers/administrators, not a student faith score. October 2026. Preserves the earlier focus on faith/reason, Catholic teaching, wonder, heritage and service while avoiding a compulsory saint/Scripture/prayer formula for every lesson. C shapes the purpose and choices; R is explicit faith teaching/reflection. Scientific inquiry remains evidence-based.

    Local planning criteria¶

    Lesson-quality criterion 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Quality
    Faith and empirical reasoning distinguished Religious claim presented as experimental proof, or science misstated Connection named but distinction unclear Scientifically accurate evidence and Catholic reflection distinguished Teacher background anticipates a misconception and models a careful source/evidence response
    Catholic purpose affects work No connection or prayer alone General value named without a classroom decision Students consider a specific dignity, stewardship, truth or service choice Choice is revisited using results, user needs or a tradeoff
    Source accuracy Invented/misattributed standard, quotation or Church claim Source question marked but not yet resolved Primary source checked, quoted/paraphrased accurately and linked Appropriate context and limits are explained in teacher-friendly language
    Inquiry and wonder Questions suppressed or inquiry replaced by a craft Wonder question named but no student investigation Students observe/ask/test and reflect without forced theological inference New student questions guide a feasible next investigation
    Access and evidence Participation/prayer behavior graded as belief Flexible modes named but criteria unclear Named objective assessed with individual oral/drawn/model/written evidence Results inform specific access support and next teaching

    Mark optional heritage/service extensions N/A if not relevant to that lesson; do not add points for more quotations, longer prayers or named scientists. Record dimension evidence, not a /20 total suggesting official certification. Unresolved source accuracy is a readiness blocker, not a minor score offset.

    Source pathway: Local Standards and the shared review's authoritative source record. A primary reference for faith/reason is Fides et Ratio. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for exact passage/quotation and any claimed diocesan or state requirement. This rubric is local, not an official Church standard.

    Lesson review record¶

    Lesson/date/reviewer Criterion Evidence/link Level/N/A Revision/source question
    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Useful prompts: "Which design choice respects the person using this?" "What did our test show?" "How can we avoid waste?" "What remains unknown?" Avoid "God is an engineer" as an explanatory scientific analogy. Historical biographies, devotional comparisons and scientific evidence require different source handling; consult background guides critically, not as proof.

    If assessing a student Catholic objective, use the student project rubric for taught reasoning. Never grade interior belief, awe, prayer frequency or family religious practice.

    Service-oriented STEM rubric¶

    Select this when the lesson explicitly teaches a reasoned design/service decision. Do not require every science investigation to be a deployed service project. October 2026. C is Catholic identity; R is the explicit faith teaching/reflection. A classroom prototype is not evidence of real-world impact.

    Source and age conditions¶

    Use the local Catholic standards and the verified source record. A primary source for the social-teaching themes is the USCCB themes overview. VERIFICATION REQUIRED for exact lesson paraphrases/quotations, source sections, diocesan requirements and current approval. This is a local classroom rubric, not an official USCCB/Archdiocesan scoring instrument.

    Keep beneficiaries respectfully described. Do not simulate disability, use real student medical profiles or deploy medical/assistive/structural/water-purification prototypes without qualified adult review. Ordinary academic inquiry and individual work are not less valuable or less Catholic than group outreach.

    Explicit objective/criterion 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning
    Identify a user need Names a solution without a relevant need Names user/need but link is incomplete Names a concrete user need and shows how a design choice responds Compares two choices using user constraints/feedback
    Apply taught dignity/service principle Proposed choice conflicts with the taught concern Names the principle but cannot yet connect the choice Explains how one choice respects the taught principle Explains a tradeoff and a way to address an unintended exclusion
    Explain stewardship Does not yet identify a resource consequence Names a resource but not the effect of the choice Explains a specific reuse/waste choice and consequence Compares alternatives using material/cost or test evidence
    Distinguish prototype from impact Claims a model has solved a real problem without evidence Recognizes it is a model but cannot state the limit Explains what was tested and what remains unproven for real use Suggests a safe next test or appropriate adult consultation

    Use only selected objectives. Fill in the exact grade-appropriate success condition; K can point to a saved material and explain whom a design helps. Grades 5-6 can reason about two alternatives and limitations. NE sits outside the scale. Access accommodations do not lower scores.

    Individual evidence and reflection¶

    Child Objective/code Actual explanation/choice Mode/support Level/NE Feedback
    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Ask: "Who might use it?" "What need are you addressing?" "What did the test actually show?" "Which choice avoids waste?" "Who could be left out?" Assess understanding of taught content, not motivation, charitable donations, family resources, prayer practice or interior belief.

    Service possibilities preserved from the earlier guide: classroom models of accessible tools, stewardship systems, environmental observations and helpful information designs. Partners and actual deployment are optional confirmed extensions, never prerequisites to classroom mastery.

    Thinking, communication and collaboration assessment¶

    The earlier question banks on reasoning, communication, collaboration, creativity, curiosity and ethics remain useful purposes. Select an explicitly taught objective, not a universal character score. October 2026.

    Taught objective 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning
    Justify a design choice with evidence Choice contradicts observed evidence Gives a relevant choice but evidence link is incomplete Explains the choice with the specified observed result Compares an alternative using another result or tradeoff
    Communicate a result Response does not yet convey the result Conveys part of the result Shows/tells/draws the result and relevant evidence clearly enough to interpret Adapts explanation after a clarifying question without changing the evidence
    Combine two ideas in a plan (only if an objective) Plan does not yet include either discussed idea Uses one idea, or includes both without explaining their use Identifies each idea and shows how they contribute to the plan Tests the combined plan and explains an improvement based on feedback
    Revise an artistic/design idea Change is unrelated to the purpose Relevant revision with an incomplete explanation Revises a taught visual/musical/design choice and explains its purpose Compares versions and explains an intentional effect or tradeoff
    Frame an investigable question Question cannot yet be investigated with the available evidence Question is relevant but too broad States a question answerable by the planned observation/test Refines it using results and identifies what to test next
    Explain a privacy/stewardship choice Does not yet recognize the taught concern Names the concern without linking the action Explains how a concrete choice addresses the taught concern Compares two actions and explains consequences for people/resources

    NE is not yet evidenced. Teacher read-aloud, bilingual response, gesture, scribe and motor assistance are access supports, not evidence of a lower level. Do not score smiles, spontaneous awe, public speaking confidence, written fluency, leadership, speed or active participation as subject mastery. Behavior/engagement can be noted separately for support planning without converting it into the objective's grade.

    Record and feedback¶

    Student/date Lesson/objective/local code Actual words/action Mode/support Level/NE Next prompt
    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Use Assessment Template and Local Standards. Official alignment requires verification. No general /24 total or score for apparent strength of faith.

    Student/peer reflection (not a mastery grade)¶

    Read aloud if needed: "Show one idea you changed. What result made you change it?" / "Which idea did your partner contribute?" / "What will you test next?" Peers provide a specific appreciative statement and question, not star ratings of a child's personality. Teacher checks individual concept evidence separately.

    Student project rubric¶

    October 2026 revision. Replaces the universal 100-point weighting with a small selection of criteria matched to the taught objectives. Preserve science/ engineering, faith reasoning, service, communication and reflection as possible learning purposes, not compulsory scoring categories for every project.

    Before use¶

    1. Write grade/unit/lesson, objective O1/O2, individual prompt and success condition using Assessment Template.
    2. Select 1-3 relevant criteria below; adjust Meets to the lesson's exact measurable threshold and grade prerequisites before teaching.
    3. Link the defined local standard. Official alignment requires verification, not a claim that a score meets all standards.
    4. Share expectations by showing/telling students. Offer oral, model, drawing, scribed or written evidence. Team products support, but never replace, each child's demonstration.

    Four levels¶

    Objective-linked criterion (use only if taught) 1 Beginning 2 Developing 3 Meets Expectation 4 Extends Learning
    O1 scientific observation/comparison Describes an outcome inconsistent with what was observed Names a relevant observation but comparison is incomplete Makes the specified comparison using an observed result Repeats or transfers the comparison and explains supporting evidence
    O1 fair test/engineering redesign Changes conditions without recognizing their effect Tests and suggests a change but evidence link is incomplete Uses the stated common conditions, records a result and justifies one redesign Retests the redesign and compares performance or a tradeoff using evidence
    O2 measurement/math reasoning Quantity/unit or comparison is incorrect Partly correct measure/data with a specific error remaining Measures/represents/explains using the lesson's specified quantity and unit Checks the result or uses it to justify a new comparison
    O2 algorithm/programming Sequence cannot produce intended result Sequence partly works; bug or execution evidence remains unresolved Explains/tests the intended sequence; real execution included if objective requires it Finds and tests a new correction/condition and explains the effect
    O2 artistic communication/music Chosen form/pattern does not yet convey the stated idea Artistic choice partly conveys the idea/phrase Uses the stated visual or musical choice to communicate the intended idea/phrase Revises a composition/phrase after feedback and explains the artistic effect
    O2 Catholic/ethical/service reasoning Choice does not yet address the taught dignity/stewardship principle Names the principle or user but connection to choice is incomplete Explains a concrete choice and how it respects the taught principle/user need Compares two choices and explains an evidence-informed tradeoff in light of the principle

    NE = not yet evidenced, outside the scale. Missed observation, absence, device failure or an inaccessible response mode is not Beginning. Access supports do not cap levels. A conceptual hint is recorded separately. Artistic skill is scored only for an explicit arts objective; handwriting, neatness, beautiful displays, expensive boards, confident speech, participation and family assistance are not mastery criteria. No grades for interior faith, prayer frequency, family religious practice or apparent enthusiasm.

    Individual score/evidence record¶

    Student Objective/local code Actual response/action Mode/access support Level or NE Feedback and next check
    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Do not average unrelated objectives into a pseudo-precise total. Report "Compared two bridge tests using the same span; next, explain the redesign" instead of "earned 80%, meets all C-STREAM standards." Expected-mastery checkpoints follow Local Standards: two dated observations on separate occasions, including an individual demonstration and changed context/follow-up explanation, both meeting the target. One project rating does not establish end-of-grade mastery.

    Bridge example and moderation¶

    O1: Compare two paper designs under the same span/load conditions. Meets: child names the observed result and shows which conditions stayed the same. A failed prototype can provide successful learning evidence. A team's strong bridge with no individual explanation is NE for that child's comparison. Drawings can communicate the comparison without handwriting assessment.

    Before a showcase, two teachers score the same anonymized examples using the selected criteria and resolve discrepancies. Events are optional celebrations of in-school work; a child's assessment does not depend on home construction, family attendance or purchased display materials.

    Related: Rubric Template, faith lesson-quality rubric, service reasoning, thinking/communication.

    Student Resources

    Student resources¶

    Print only what the objective needs; a board-drawn prompt or oral response is equally valid. No reading/writing prerequisite for K-1. Adult models one step and accepts point/show/build/sort/tell/dictate; each child gets their own turn.

    Resource Purpose and use
    Show, Try, Tell Actual nonreader/adult-led comparison example and reusable response route
    Journal cover Optional personalized cover; black-and-white/hand-drawn works
    Goals Interest/next-learning conversation; not an achievement grade
    Engineering process Plan/test/improve evidence; select fields, not a mandatory long worksheet
    Wonder journal Questions/observations; enjoyment stars are not mastery
    Project reflection One objective/evidence prompt at a time; full reflection optional
    Student sheet template Teacher adapts objective, prompt, criterion and evidence mode

    Use assessment and rubrics for individual learning. Do not grade participation, handwriting, neatness or apparent faith as subject mastery. Arts skills are assessed only if explicit objectives; A includes music and M means mathematics. Named records follow the school's actual privacy practice. Local standard definitions: Local Standards; official alignment/source questions require verification.

    Show, Try, Tell¶

    Teacher/substitute: This is an adult-led card, not independent reading. Use it with the actual lesson objective and kit. A printed copy is optional. Draw the three boxes on the board or place three real objects as visual cues. Say ONE step, show it, let the child do it, then repeat. No homework.

    1. SHOW
    Adult points to the object.

    Child points, sorts or draws here.
    2. TRY
    Adult models one action.

    Child builds, tests or moves a large pointer.
    3. TELL
    Adult shows the result.

    Child points, gestures, tells or dictates.

    Ready-to-use comparison example (K/nonreader)¶

    Objective: "I can show which of two objects is longer." Materials: Two ordinary school pencils of visibly different lengths, each child's familiar drawing tool/paper optional. No small new parts or devices.

    1. Hold up the two pencils. Say "Look." Put them side by side with ends aligned.
    2. Model pointing along a pencil. Say "Show the longer one." Let each child point.
    3. Reverse left/right order, realign ends. Say "Show me again. How do you know?" Accept tracing, pointing at the unmatched end, gesture or words; adult scribes.

    Meets: Child identifies the longer pencil in both placements and indicates the unmatched end/aligned comparison. If position alone determines the answer, model aligned ends and recheck later. Do not score reading, handwriting or speech. This is a local classroom criterion, not a verified official benchmark.

    Support: Larger objects, extra wait time, adult holds objects steady, child uses gaze/gesture or home-language response. Challenge: Compare a third object and explain the order. Catholic connection: Care for shared tools and use them fairly; no scientific proof claim or forced comparison of God to an engineer. Safety: No sharpening/swinging; keep tools at desk level.

    Adapt to the planned lesson¶

    Teacher writes/reads objective [ ], actual question [ ], Meets condition [ ] and local code from Local Standards [ ]. Use real-object demonstration for build/test or large arrow cards for sequences. Keep each student's own turn; do not accept a partner's answer as their evidence.

    Child/date Exact action/words Objective Access support Level/NE Next check
    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]

    Use Assessment Template and Student Sheet for teacher records.

    About

    👋 About the Author¶

    Joe Vandermark¶

    With more than 30 years in technology, I'm passionate about helping people understand how computers, cloud systems, and new tools make life and work better. I created the C-STREAM Framework to bring that same spirit of innovation into Catholic education—nurturing both the mind and spirit.

    My Philosophy

    STREAM learning gives every student the confidence to explore, ask questions, and build the future with both skill and heart.

    💼 Professional Background¶

    Technology Leadership¶

    At Microsoft, I lead a team of Cloud Solution Architects who help companies build safe and creative solutions in the cloud. I've also authored two books on building strong, people-focused teams.

    Entrepreneurship & Wellness¶

    I'm a franchise owner and Chief Operating Officer for The Vital Stretch in the Twin Cities, where I'm building wellness studios that help people move better and stay healthy. I love connecting technology, business, wellness, and community in meaningful ways.

    Education & Service¶

    I volunteer as a STEM teacher at Our Lady of the Prairie Catholic School, where I help students discover how creativity, science, faith, and problem-solving work together. My background includes:

    • Serving on a school board
    • Advising early-stage startups
    • Studies in computer science, business systems, and Catholic formation

    ⛪ Faith & Service¶

    • Chair of the Minnesota Knights of Columbus Student Loan Fund, supporting students across the state
    • 10+ years serving on the board of Catholic Youth Camp
    • Bringing that same spirit of service into every classroom

    👨‍👩‍👦‍👦 Family¶

    🤝 Contributing to C-STREAM

    Catholic Science, Technology, Religion, Engineering, Arts, and Math

    Thank you for your interest in contributing to the C-STREAM Framework! We welcome your input, whether it's submitting new lesson plans, improving existing resources, or helping us better integrate Catholic values into STEM education.

    Before editing curriculum, read the curriculum review, local standards and teaching-release priorities. Preserve baseline findings when recording a revision; a changed file is not automatically classroom-ready.

    📋 How to Contribute¶

    1. 🐛 Reporting Issues¶

    If you notice any issues with the framework, lesson plans, templates, or resources (e.g., broken links, typos, or inaccuracies), please help us by reporting them:

    1. Go to the Issues tab in the repository
    2. Click on New Issue
    3. Provide a clear description with as much detail as possible:
    4. The file where the issue exists
    5. What needs to be corrected
    6. Any suggested fixes

    2. 📝 Submitting New Lesson Plans¶

    We'd love your help creating new C-STREAM lessons! Follow these steps:

    1. Fork the Repository
      Fork this repository to your own GitHub account.

    2. Create a New Branch
      Create a branch specific to your changes: 

      git checkout -b add-new-lesson-plan

    3. Use Our Templates
      Build your lesson using the C-STREAM Lesson Plan Template. Ensure your lesson:

    4. Integrates faith and reason (the "R" in C-STREAM)
    5. Specifies grade-appropriate timing (K: 25min, 1-2: 30min, 3-4: 40min, 5-6: 45min)
    6. Includes materials from the CSCOE Library where applicable

    7. Connects to Catholic values and/or Catholic Social Teaching

    8. Submit a Pull Request
      Submit a pull request to the main branch with a clear description of your lesson.

    3. ✨ Improving Existing Resources¶

    If you have suggestions for improving current materials:

    1. Identify the Resource
      Locate the file in the appropriate folder (Templates/, Rubrics/, Resources/)

    2. Fork and Branch
      Fork the repository and create a branch

    3. Make Changes
      Edit to improve clarity, expand activities, or better integrate Catholic values. Be sure to reference:

    4. CSCOE Library materials where appropriate
    5. Grade-level time frames

    6. The 12 Success Factors outlined in the framework

    7. Submit a Pull Request
      Include a description of what you changed and why

    4. 👨‍🔬 Adding Catholic Scientist Profiles¶

    Help expand our Catholic Scientists Heritage resource:

    1. Research a Catholic scientist not yet profiled
    2. Include:
    3. Biographical information
    4. Scientific contributions
    5. Faith journey and how faith influenced their work
    6. Discussion questions for students
    7. Grade-level adaptations

    5. 📦 Contributing CSCOE Library Integration¶

    If you have experience with CSCOE Library materials:

    • Share lesson ideas using specific equipment

    • Document setup procedures for materials

    • Suggest alternative activities when materials aren't available

    ✅ Contribution Guidelines¶

    Respect Catholic Values¶

    All lesson plans, resources, and materials must align with Catholic values and teachings. C-STREAM is built on the foundation that faith and reason are complementary.

    Maintain Grade Appropriateness¶

    Grade Time Approach
    Kindergarten 25 min Wonder, exploration, simple hands-on
    Grades 1-2 30 min Guided exploration with structure
    Grades 3-4 40 min Independent work with collaboration
    Grades 5-6 45 min Complex projects, student-led inquiry

    Follow the 12 Success Factors¶

    Ensure contributions align with the 12 Success Factors for Catholic STEM education.

    Use Consistent Formatting¶

    • Follow existing file naming conventions

    • Use provided templates

    • Include proper YAML frontmatter

    • Add breadcrumb navigation

    Test Your Contributions¶

    If contributing a new lesson plan:

    • Test in a classroom setting if possible

    • Note any challenges or modifications needed

    • Include setup time and preparation requirements

    Also provide exact, scalable supplies for 10/15/20/25 students, numbered steps within the native period, an individual objective-linked evidence check, visible safety/stop rules, support/challenge, cleanup and an indoor alternative when weather matters. For early readers, demonstrate directions and accept oral, drawn or manipulated evidence.

    Use hands-on/unplugged methods first. Categorize technology as None, Optional, Recommended or Required and explain any required use. A device-free fallback must state what changes in the objective; it cannot certify actual hardware/software execution. Family work and donations must not be prerequisites.

    Update the curriculum maps¶

    Add/update the corresponding band-audit CSV in Review/ for every lesson. Use the documented schema, the actual schedule/rotation, the native period as integer minutes per meeting, and 2-5 relevant local codes linked to planned individual evidence. Keep the baseline status/priority and record the subsequent revision separately.

    From the repository root:

    .\scripts\Build-CurriculumMaps.ps1
.\scripts\Build-CurriculumMaps.ps1 -ValidateOnly
mkdocs build

    Include the regenerated maps with the curriculum change. Schema validation does not establish safety, developmental fit or standards mastery. Report desk walkthroughs and actual classroom trials separately.

    For current Kindergarten version-3.0 references, keep metadata, actual teaching steps and the individual-evidence definitions in the K sync script consistent:

    .\scripts\Sync-KindergartenAudit.ps1
.\scripts\Test-KindergartenReferences.ps1
.\scripts\Build-CurriculumMaps.ps1

    The K validator checks the current 37-document/29-autonomous-reference contract, 25-minute sequences and supply scaling. An intentional structural revision must update the corresponding contract/tests, not merely bypass their failures.

    Verify sources and claims¶

    Use authoritative sources and record the URL, applicable version and review date. Official benchmark alignment needs the exact benchmark, student task and assessment evidence. Label locally created standards as local. Unverified Church/history/Archdiocesan/state/accreditation claims are VERIFICATION REQUIRED; do not invent identifiers or quotations.

    Integrate Faith Meaningfully¶

    Don't just add a prayer at the beginning—weave Catholic identity throughout like "yeast that causes everything to rise."

    🔄 Review Process¶

    Once your pull request is submitted:

    1. Initial Review - The C-STREAM team reviews your contribution
    2. Feedback - You may receive suggestions for improvements
    3. Revision - Update your pull request based on feedback
    4. Merge - Approved contributions are merged into the main branch
    5. Recognition - Contributors are acknowledged in release notes

    💡 Ideas for Contributions¶

    Not sure where to start? Here are some ideas:

    • Add more Catholic scientist profiles

    • Create grade-specific activity variations

    • Develop Digital Art/Music integration lessons

    • Write family engagement activities

    • Translate resources to Spanish

    • Create video tutorials for complex setups

    • Document CSCOE equipment procedures

    • Develop assessment tools

    • Add seasonal/liturgical connections

    📫 Questions?¶

    If you have questions about contributing:

    • Open a Discussion in the repository

    • Review existing Issues for similar questions

    • Contact the C-STREAM team through GitHub

    🙏 Thank You!¶

    Your contributions help us continue to inspire students to explore STEM through a Catholic lens. Together, we can help students see how science and faith work together to understand God's amazing creation.

    "Science and faith are complementary – the beautiful harmony of faith and reason so students can be a light in the secular world."

    Happy Teaching and Creating! ✨
